title: The Walkthrough: booking desk + self-qualification
question: Your steer, three ways: the desk look stays; what changes is where the fit check sits against the calendar. Lock one, steer again, or re-roll.

options.label: Questions lead to the desk
options.thesis: Qualification comes first; the calendar waits at the end of the page, on the desk.
materials: calendar on the desk at the close
options.viewport: Offer at left, the report standing on the miniature desk at right; 'Is this a fit?' with three check rows starts right below; the calendar desk closes the page.
options.risk: Ready-to-book referrals have to scroll to the calendar; the header and hero buttons must jump there cleanly.

options.label: A fit card on the desk
options.thesis: The card on the desk asks three questions, then turns into the calendar.
materials: fit card with Yes / Not yet pills
options.viewport: The booking desk you liked, but the card starts as 'Before you pick a time' with three checks and 'Show me times'; a kind not-a-fit note sits at its foot.
options.risk: Real friction in the first viewport; without JavaScript the page must still show the questions and the plain Cal link.

options.label: The desk stays with you
options.thesis: The desk and calendar stay pinned while the fit questions scroll past and tick off.
options.viewport: Past the opening, the left column walks the three fit lines as big check blocks while the desk and calendar hold on the right with a progress pill.
options.risk: Self-qualification by reading is soft friction; tightening it later means adding a gate to a layout that didn't plan one.
